source_doubts.where: Theorem 1.2 (the external input), source 'The exact existence input'; rewrite Theorem 1.2, Remark 1.3 and checklist item 1
source_doubts.quote:
There exist a finite field $K_2$ of characteristic two, a finitely
generated group $H_2$, and finite sums $a_2,b_2\in K_2[H_2]$ with
$a_2b_2=1$ and $b_2a_2\ne1$.
source_doubts.problem: This is the only unproved step in both documents, and the whole result rests on it. It is taken by citation from a companion paper and asserts a group algebra over a finite field that is not directly finite, i.e. a counterexample to Kaplansky's direct finiteness conjecture; it would also force H_2 to be non-sofic. The source itself says it uses 'the existence theorem, not an executed numerical instance or a group-word decision procedure', so nothing in either document lets a reader check it. Everything after this input (Lemma 2.1 through the proof of Theorem 1.1) checks out step by step, so Theorem 1.1 is established only conditionally. The rewrite keeps the statement verbatim and says in prose (Remark 1.3, the abstract, the checklist) that it is cited and unchecked, but it does not put an \unverified{...} box on it; the checklist's remark that no box appears because no proved step raised a doubt should not be read as covering this input.
